chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khakan said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (the third Imam), peace be upon him, perform the prostration of gratitude, so he spread his forearms and pressed his chest and belly against the ground. I asked him about that, and he said, 'Thus it is obligatory.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct physical posture for the prostration of gratitude (sujud al-shukr) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the physical distinctiveness of the prostration of gratitude (sujud al-shukr), where the Imam pressed his chest and belly fully to the ground to express profound thankfulness. While the Imam declared this specific posture 'obligatory' (kadha yajibu), Shia scholars often interpret this as establishing the recommended excellence (mustahabb) or the specific manner of the Imam rather than a universal legal obligation for all believers, distinguishing it from the standard prostration in prayer.
